extracted.intended_audience: scientists and researchers preparing public comments on regulatory rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for scientists to draft concise, evidence-based public comments for agency rulemaking dockets — showing expertise, citing research, and linking arguments to agency mission/statutes. Emphasizes structure, identification, and usability for agency staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core principle: unique, fact-based, and succinct
rubrics_metrics.description: The most valuable public comments are unique, fact-based, and succinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientists should leverage their ability to synthesize data and research as a key strength; prioritize presenting novel, factual contributions rather than repetition or broad opinion. Keep comments concise to aid agency reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report Scientific Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Present data supporting or opposing the regulation's underlying theory to strengthen the agency's scientific foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on evidence that bears directly on the regulation's assumptions or predicted effects; provide data summaries that clarify how the evidence supports or contradicts the regulatory rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Proper Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a heading that states the regulation name and the docket ID number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place clear identification (regulation title and docket ID) at the top of the comment to demonstrate you reviewed the correct rulemaking and to ensure your submission is properly associated in the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Open with a sentence identifying yourself and relevant expertise on the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a concise credential statement (e.g., job title, affiliation, area of expertise) so agency staff can quickly assess the commenter's subject-matter authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summarize Research First
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin with a discussion-style summary of your data before expanding on details for easier agency response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a high-level summary of findings and their implications; follow with detailed methods, data, and analyses for staff who need deeper information. This structure helps agency reviewers grasp the key message quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify Implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate how your research relates to the regulation rather than leaving inferences to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the regulatory relevance of your results (e.g., how a finding affects compliance costs, risks, benefits, or the scientific assumption underlying the rule). Avoid leaving the connection implicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific paper citations to help agency staff locate references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full citations (and links if available) to primary literature, datasets, or technical reports you rely on so reviewers can verify and follow up on evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect to Agency Mission and Statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference the agency's mission statement and relevant statutes to strengthen your argument's alignment with their mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame comments in terms of how the evidence advances or conflicts with statutory obligations or the agency's stated mission to make your recommendations more actionable and persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Available Resources (templates, exemplars, alerts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage provided templates, featured exemplary comments, blog stories, and email alerts for structural guidance and tracking agency responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult comment templates for structure, read exemplary comments to model tone and content, learn from scientists' impact stories, and sign up for Regulations.gov alerts to monitor agency responses and follow-up opportunities.
